reason: Smaers 2017 primary_visual_gray is not a Smaers measurement: it is de Sousa et al. 2010 [S6], which is itself Frahm et al. 1984 area striata grey matter. Value-matched EXACT (14 spp, 0.0% difference; e.g. Homo 14.787 = Frahm 14787 mm3, Cercopithecus ascanius 4.272 = 4272, Gorilla 12.062 = 12062). Taking it would republish Frahm 1984 under a 2017 date.

Smaers 2017 primary_visual_white is Frahm et al. 1984 area striata WHITE matter republished, not a Smaers measurement (EXACT value-match, e.g. Homo 5.439 = Frahm 5439 mm3, Pan troglodytes 4.004 = 4004). Same reasoning as the grey-matter column.

Smaers 2017 prefrontal_gray is Smaers et al. 2011 Suppl. Table 2 republished (anterior section-5, summed L+R; human = mean of 8), 19/11 spp within 2%. Add Smaers_etal_2011_SupplementaryTable1 to the selection if you want prefrontal volumes; do not date this measurement 2017.
Smaers 2017 prefrontal_white is Smaers et al. 2011 Suppl. Table 2 republished, same as the grey-matter column. Use the 2011 raw table as the source if prefrontal volumes are wanted.

other_association_gray is not measured. Per the 2017 supplement it is neocortex - frontal lobe - primary visual, i.e. an arithmetic residual of de Sousa 2010 + Stephan 1981 values that are already in this merge. Importing it would double-count them; recompute from the primaries instead if the quantity is needed.

other_association_white is the white-matter counterpart of the same derived residual (neocortex - frontal lobe - primary visual). Not a measurement; recompute from the primaries rather than importing it.

frontal_motor_gray is the only genuinely 2017-unique numeric column, so it is kept - but it is the POSTERIOR section-5 of 20 frontal sections and was never published anywhere else, so it cannot be checked against any public table. It is a biased anterior/posterior proxy, not the true premotor border. Treat as provisional.

frontal_motor_white is the white-matter counterpart of the same unpublished posterior section-5 partition: 2017-unique, kept, but unverifiable against any public table and a proxy rather than a true premotor border.

This comes from volumes_compiled.R (same line, same result in the canonical volumes_long.csv), so it is an upstream issue, NOT something this selection introduced. Here it only reaches the 13 species Stephan 1981 does not cover, because mass_rule pins the rest to Stephan. Set action to skip, or fix the reshape upstream, once decided.

reason: Stephan 1981 prints 0 for the nucleus tractus olfactorius in several catarrhines. Per the Stephan 1987 data dictionary a printed 0 means 'not determinable with certainty', not a true zero - volumes_compiled.R maps it to NA for the 1987 table but leaves the 1981 zeros standing, and so does this script (5 species end up with NTO = 0). Decide whether the 1981 zeros are sentinels too before using this variable; contrast Bulbus_olfactorius_accessorius, whose zeros in catarrhines are real absences.
